questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Polynomials
questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(0)y(0)+x(2)y(2)+x(3)y(3).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=5-3t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=5-3t,$ we obtain

$$
p(0)=5,\,p(2)=-1,\,p(3)=-4.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(0)p(0)+p(2)p(2)+p(3)p(3)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(0)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}+[p(3)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(5)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25+1+16} \\  & =\sqrt{42}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Continuous Functions
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[0,\pi ]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,\pi ],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\,{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\,({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2}){|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(\pi -\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi }{2})-(0-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡0}{2}) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we made use of the trigonometric identities

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t=1\,\text{and}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖f(t)‖ & =\sqrt{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Polynomials
questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2)+x(3)y(3).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=2-t+{t}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=2-t+{t}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
p(1)=2,\,p(2)=4,\,p(3)=8.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(1)p(1)+p(2)p(2)+p(3)p(3)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(1)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}+[p(3)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+16+64} \\  & =\sqrt{84} \\  & =2\sqrt{21}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Continuous Functions
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[-\pi ,\pi ]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[-\pi ,\pi ],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\,{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\,({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2}){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =(\pi +\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi }{2})-((-\pi )+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(-2\pi )}{2}) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we made use of the trigonometric identities

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t=1\,\text{and}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖f(t)‖ & =\sqrt{2\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Normalizing a Vector in an Inner Product Space
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Normalize the vector $f(t)=t-{t}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{(t-{t}^{2})}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\,({t}^{2}-2{t}^{3}+{t}^{4}),\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{t}^{4}}{2}+\frac{{t}^{5}}{5})|}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{30}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
‖f(t)‖=\frac{1}{\sqrt{30}}.
$$

To normalize the vector $f(t),$ we divide $f(t)$ by its norm $‖f(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{f(t)}{‖f(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{(t-{t}^{2})}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{30}}} \\  & =\sqrt{30}(t-{t}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$
